sec: Contraindications, puncture sites and measured vs derived parameters · p827

items.q: Match the contraindications for ABG puncture — 1) Vascular test  2) Local factor  3) Systemic vascular disease  4) Vasospastic disorder … A) Active Raynaud's syndrome  B) Abnormal Allen's test  C) Severe peripheral vascular artery disease  D) Local infection or distorted anatomy at the puncture site
items.exp: Contraindications: abnormal Allen's test; local infection or distorted anatomy at the puncture site; severe peripheral vascular artery disease; active Raynaud's syndrome. (Book p827)

items.q: A patient's Allen's test is abnormal but the radial pulse is easily felt. What does the chapter advise?
opts: Avoid the puncture — an abnormal Allen's test is a listed contraindication
Proceed with a 90° puncture for a quicker sample
Proceed but use a larger 5 ml syringe instead
Proceed and ignore the test if the ulnar pulse is palpable
items.exp: An abnormal Allen's test is the first printed contraindication to ABG puncture. (Book p827)

items.q: Match the puncture sites printed — 1) First-listed site  2) Thigh-level site  3) Arm sites  4) Foot site … A) Dorsalis pedis  B) Radial artery  C) Brachial and axillary arteries  D) Femoral artery
items.exp: Site of puncture list: radial artery, femoral artery, brachial artery, axillary artery and dorsalis pedis. (Book p827)

items.q: Which site of puncture is listed first in the chapter?
items.exp: The list begins with the radial artery, followed by femoral, brachial, axillary and dorsalis pedis. (Book p827)

items.q: Match the ABG parameters — 1) Measured parameters  2) Derived parameters  3) Example of a derived parameter set … A) HCO₃⁻, anion gap and base excess  B) pH, pCO₂, pO₂, cCa²⁺, cCl⁻, cK⁺, cNa⁺, cGlucose and hematocrit  C) HCO₃⁻ only
items.exp: Measured: pH, pCO₂, pO₂, cCa²⁺, cCl⁻, cK⁺, cNa⁺, cGlucose and hematocrit. Derived: HCO₃⁻, anion gap and base excess. (Book p827)

items.q: All but one of these are listed as MEASURED (not derived) ABG parameters. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Base excess belongs to the derived group with HCO₃⁻ and the anion gap; cCa²⁺, cGlucose and hematocrit are all measured directly. (Book p827)

items.q: ‘HCO₃⁻ is a measured parameter on the blood gas analyzer, whereas pH is derived from it.’
opts: False — HCO₃⁻ is derived, while pH is measured
True — HCO₃⁻ is measured and pH is derived
False — both HCO₃⁻ and pH are derived
True, but only when base excess is also reported
items.exp: The arrow runs from measured (pH, pCO₂, pO₂, electrolytes, glucose, hematocrit) to derived (HCO₃⁻, anion gap, base excess). (Book p827)
